title: Investigation continues in Fort St. John RCMP custody death
article: Details remain sparse surrounding the case of a man who died in RCMP custody in Fort St. John last August.
Police are still not releasing the man's name, age or place of residence at the request of his family, Const. Annie Linteau of Vancouver-based RCMP E Division Strategic Communications said Thursday.

"We are continuing our investigation and we're just awaiting a review by a use-of-force expert, and that's something that's always done in any in-custody death investigation," said Linteau, adding that no timeline has been set for completion of the review. "There are few (use-of-force) experts, so we're just awaiting someone to be available."

According to an RCMP press release late last August, the man went into cardiac arrest while struggling with RCMP members. The officers were attempting to restrain the man using a Ripp Hobble device, which is a nylon belt that can be tied around a person's elbows, knees and ankles to restrain the leg movement of a combative individual.
Police say the man had been combative, kicking and biting the officers, after they found him yelling and banging on windows in downtown Fort St. John around 1 a.m. on Aug. 28, 2006.
The body of the deceased man, who RCMP say was in his 30s, was transported to Kamloops for a forensic autopsy.

Both the autopsy report and a toxicology report will not be released to the public until a coroner's inquest is conducted into the death, according to the B.C. Coroner's Service. But, Shane DeMeyer, the regional coroner based in Prince George, said an inquest has not yet been scheduled.
"Being an in-custody death, very likely this is going to go to (a coroner's) inquest," DeMeyer said Thursday. "There hasn't been a formal decision on that yet, but that's the usual route."
The North District Major Crime Unit is involved in the investigation.
